Rugged tablet for Eworks Manager

Eworks Manager is job management software for trades and service businesses, sold from the UK by Eworks Manager Limited, a company registered in England and Wales under number 08916129 with a registered office at 107 Cheapside, London, and a Manchester address on its Google Play developer listing. The vendor describes it as one platform that connects the office and the field: job logging and scheduling, team tracking, compliance and certificate storage, quoting, invoicing, inventory and asset management. Its site lists electricians, plumbers, gas engineers, fire safety engineers, security installers, HVAC, facilities management, cleaning and construction among the trades it serves. The office works in a web-based admin system; field workers receive and complete jobs in the Eworks mobile app.

The mobile app is where site work happens. The vendor's Google Play listing says job sheets can be assigned from the admin system or the app, that photos and signatures can be attached to jobs, that quotes and invoices can be created on the move, and that a tracker shows the office how staff are progressing on location. The vendor's mobile app page says the app works offline, saving to the device and uploading when the worker is next online, and that it can be installed on a team's phones or tablets. Its Sage Marketplace listing adds digital documents such as gas certificates and EICRs, questionnaires completed on a job, stock checks and picking lists, and a barcode scanner that finds an asset straight from the camera. That is a device that rides in a van, goes into plant rooms and roof spaces, and gets handed to a customer to sign, which is where a consumer tablet tends to fail early.

This page sets out what Eworks Manager publishes about the devices its app runs on, which Tuga rugged tablets meet those published requirements, where the Windows option fits and where it does not, and how a UK contractor can buy a single trial unit before committing to a fleet.

Requirements

What Eworks Manager needs from a device

Each item below comes from Eworks Manager Limited's own listing or documentation, with the source linked.

  • Android 7.0 or later, from the Google Play listing

    The vendor publishes no system requirements page. The only published Android figure is in the Google Play listing for the Eworks app (package com.eworksmanager.ewm3, developer Eworks Manager Limited), which when checked on 19 October 2026 showed version 5.0.16, updated 20 September 2026, with a minimum API level of 24 (Android 7.0) and a target API level of 36. The listing is free, rated PEGI 3, is marked as sharing location, and its data safety section lists location and photos and videos among the data collected. No RAM or storage figure is published anywhere by the vendor. For context, the App Store listing requires iOS 15.6 or iPadOS 15.6 or later. Source: play.google.com

  • Android app installed on phones or tablets

    The vendor's mobile app page says the app is free to download from the Apple App Store and Google Play, that you search for Eworks Manager, install it on your team's phones or tablets, and log in with existing Eworks details. The App Store version is described as designed for iPad, so a tablet layout is one the vendor publishes for. The vendor gives no screen size guidance and no list of supported tablet models. Source: eworksmanager.co.uk

  • Offline working, saving to the device and uploading when back online

    The vendor's mobile app FAQ says the app even works offline, saving to the device and uploading when workers are next online. Its mobile documents page repeats this and says to use the mobile workforce app anywhere with offline mode. The vendor does not publish how much data is cached on the device, how long jobs take to arrive, or any limit on what can be done without signal, and its Mobile App Policy says personal data may be stored on the device in application data caches. Source: eworksmanager.co.uk

  • Digital job sheets, certificates, questionnaires, photos and customer signatures

    The Google Play description says photos and signatures can be attached to jobs and that job sheets can be assigned to projects from the admin system or the app. The vendor's site describes digital job sheets, checklists and sign-offs completed on site, with electrical safety certificates and gas safety certificates stored in one place, and says photos, videos and customer signatures give workers proof of what they did and when. The Sage Marketplace listing names gas certificates, EICR and fire detection and alarm certificates as digital documents, and says questionnaires can be set for the Eworks app while on a job. The vendor publishes no requirement for a stylus or a minimum screen size for signing. Source: us-marketplace.sage.com

  • Asset barcode scanning through the camera

    The Sage Marketplace listing says that with the barcode scanner you can search for your assets straight from the camera on your mobile devices, and that scanning an asset's barcode opens that asset so an operative can update its status, add notes or change its location. The vendor's facilities management page says you can barcode and locate your assets using the system. No support for a dedicated hardware scan engine, an external scanner or NFC tags is documented, so on any device the scan path the vendor describes is the camera. The vendor does not publish which barcode or QR formats are read. Source: eworksmanager.co.uk

  • Location tracking from the app, with permission

    The vendor's Mobile App Policy says the app uses location tracking for the functions that require it, that users consent to it for those functions only, and that location data can be turned off in device settings. The real-time tracking page says the office can see where every field worker is in real time and that tracking can be turned off outside working hours. The Google Play listing is marked as sharing location. No GNSS accuracy or location hardware requirement is published. Source: eworksmanager.co.uk

  • Windows: no Windows app, web-based admin system in a browser

    The vendor publishes no Windows app and its Mobile App Policy describes the app as hosted on the Google Play store and Apple store only. The product's two parts are described in its Sage Marketplace listing as a web-based admin system and a mobile app, and the vendor's own site calls it cloud-based software. No supported browser list, browser versions or desktop operating system requirements are published. Source: ca-marketplace.sage.com

Setting up

Getting Eworks Manager running

  1. Ask your Eworks Manager administrator to set the field worker up as a user in your Eworks account, and to allocate the digital documents, questionnaires and asset registers your team will use on site.
  2. On the Tuga A10, A8 or A6, open Google Play, search for Eworks Manager and install the Eworks app (package com.eworksmanager.ewm3, developer Eworks Manager Limited), then sign in with the worker's Eworks details.
  3. Allow camera and location access when prompted. The camera is the documented path for asset barcode scanning and job photos, and the vendor's Mobile App Policy says location tracking is used only for the functions that need it and can be turned off in device settings.
  4. Before the first job without signal, keep the device online long enough for the worker's jobs to sync. The vendor says the app saves to the device offline and uploads when next online, but publishes no figure for how much is cached, so test a job end to end offline before relying on it.
  5. Test a complete job on one device: open a job sheet, scan an asset barcode that is already in your asset register, attach a photo, complete a questionnaire or certificate, and capture a customer signature, then confirm it all arrives in the admin system.
  6. On a Tuga W10, open the Eworks admin system in Edge or Chrome and keep the browser updated. Use it for office work; it will not run the mobile app.
  7. Fit the tempered glass screen protector before the device goes out. For the A10 and A8, add the vehicle mounting dock in the van; for the A10 and W10, add the charging dock where devices live overnight; for the A6, add the belt holster.
  8. Roll out to the rest of the team only after the trial device has completed real jobs for a week, including at least one site with no signal.

Questions

Eworks Manager on a Tuga device

The vendor publishes no system requirements page, so the only published device figure is the Google Play listing's minimum API level of 24 (Android 7.0). The Tuga A10 runs Android 14 with Google Play and has 8GB RAM and 128GB storage, so it meets that figure. The Tuga A8 (Android 12, 6GB RAM) and Tuga A6 (Android 15, 4GB RAM) also meet it. We do not describe any device as certified or tested by Eworks Manager; these are the vendor's published requirements set against the device specifications.

The vendor's mobile app FAQ says the app works offline, saving to the device and uploading when workers are next online. It does not publish how much is cached, how long new jobs take to reach a device or what cannot be done offline, so run a test job without signal before relying on it. The A10, A8 and A6 all run the Google Play app. A Tuga W10 can only use the web-based admin system in a browser, and the vendor does not document offline working there.

The vendor's Sage Marketplace listing says the barcode scanner finds an asset straight from the camera on a mobile device, and that scanning opens the asset so its status, notes or location can be updated. The A10, A8 and A6 all have a 13MP rear camera with flash, and on each of them scanning runs through the camera via the app. The A6 also has a Zebra 2D scan engine, but the vendor documents no dedicated scan engine or external scanner support, so do not buy it for that reason alone.

Both meet the published Android requirement. The A10 has more RAM (8GB against 6GB), a sharper 1920 x 1200 screen for multi-page certificates and questionnaires, IP68 against IP67, and MIL-STD-810H, which the A8 does not have. The A8 has a 1000 nit screen against the A10's 350 nits, a removable battery, VESA mount points, and costs £379 against £449. Workers who mostly work outdoors or do long days away from a charger may prefer the A8; those filling in long documents or working in wetter, harder conditions are better served by the A10.
